slope: Ground steeper than 10° tips the lander over. Check the Slope bar before you commit.
cold: When the Sun is gone for more than 100 hours, batteries run out and heaters stop. Check 'Longest dark': long nights freeze landers.
blackout: Earth can sit below the horizon near the pole. After more than 72 hours without a link, the mission is lost. Check 'Longest blackout'.
low_sun: Solar panels need sunlight to make power. A site that stays dark for too long leaves the lander without energy. Needs the Sun at least 50% of the week.
low_comm: The Earth link depends on how much of the time Earth is above the horizon. Poor visibility means a patchy link with mission control. Needs Earth in view at least 50% of the week.
win: Well done! You balanced slope, sunlight, long nights and the Earth link, and the lander survived until the end of its window.
dark_landing: Pilots and landing cameras need light to see the ground. With the Sun below about 5°, the landing site is still in darkness or in very long shadows. Apollo waited for local sunrise.
glare_landing: With the Sun high in the sky there are no shadows, and rocks and craters look flat. Apollo landed with the Sun only 5-14° up so long shadows showed every boulder.
